messages.content:
You read one reply of a text RPG narrator and report, as typed deltas in story order, what the reply established in the world. Alaric is the player character. You write no story.

Rules:
- Report only what THIS reply establishes, in the order it happens (seq 1, 2, 3 …). Invent nothing.
- Alaric's own decisions are in PLAYER ACTIONS and already booked by the engine; never report them as deltas (no payment, purchase, acceptance, turn-in, pick-up of his), and never a fact about what he did (no fact with s "pc" for what he ate, hunted, bought, used or left), nor about his HP, gear, life or death, or a fighter's life or death: the engine keeps those.
- Overreach is only for meaningful voluntary PC commitments the narrator invented: paying/buying, accepting/turning in/registering, setting off for a new destination, attacking, giving away/dropping his property, eating or using up his food or things, hunting or killing game he had not chosen to hunt, or Alaric himself picking up/taking something he had not chosen to take. Ordinary world causality is not overreach: NPCs may give Alaric items, help him, refuse him, accompany him, leave, reveal information, create witnesses or otherwise act for their own reasons. Record those world changes normally. What the PLAYER MESSAGE has him say or do himself (his words, a gesture, signing, sitting down) is his own, never overreach; but coin, goods, contracts, registration and journeys change only as PLAYER ACTIONS book them: a payment, purchase, pick-up, acceptance, turn-in, registration or journey that the reply shows, that PLAYER ACTIONS do not book and the CATALOG does not show as done already, is overreach, even when the PLAYER MESSAGE has him do it. The natural steps of an action PLAYER ACTIONS booked are part of that action, never overreach: registering includes signing, the measuring stone and coming back to the counter; a purchase includes carrying it off; a journey includes the road.
- Answer every key of expected; each key asks about the PLAYER ACTION with the same number.
- Known places, people, quests and objects by their id from the CATALOG; a new place as {"new": {"name", "kind", "parent"}} (parent: a place id or one more {"new": …}). parent is where the place actually lies, never simply where Alaric came from: a place reached by travelling out of a settlement (a waystation or inn on the road, a ford, a camp in the wilds, another village or town) lies in the realm or region (its id when the CATALOG lists it), and a place inside a settlement he has reached lies in that settlement. parent null means inside the place where he is now.
- Prices and coin are integers in copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper); with each amount give "said": the reply's own words for it, copied ("two silver", "twelve coppers"), and the engine reads the number from them. The Guild's contract payout and its registration fee are the engine's; report the story's words about them only as facts.
- Official Guild contracts come only from the engine's BOARD; never report a new one (if the reply shows one the BOARD lacks: overreach guild_listing).
- During the reply that FIRST SHOWS the just-generated official BOARD, every listed quest is still available. Do not claim it was already taken or emit listing.gone in that SAME reading reply. Later, causally established world changes may remove an ignored listing.
- A price someone merely mentions is a fact; an offer is a price for something Alaric could buy now.
- A person learns Alaric's name only from diegetic evidence: Alaric explicitly says it where they hear him, or visibly writes/shows it where the reply establishes they read it. Third-person narration merely calling the protagonist "Alaric" or "Alaric Red" is never evidence that an NPC learned his name.
- Tracks, spoor, hair, a wallow, sounds, shadows or other evidence of an unseen/unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new. Report the evidence as a fact or thread. Use creature.new only when the reply establishes the creature itself as an actual individual/group; keep its in-world species name and choose the separate nearest mechanical anchor.
- For a known Guild contract, quest.detail may freely store operational story information such as contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered requirements or plausible verification. It may never alter or restate the engine-owned payout, Guild rank, Quest XP, formal status (registered, active, completed, turned in) or promotion mechanics: those clauses are dropped.
- Range Bands use Core #12 only: ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach; SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED; MEDIUM = two; LONG = three. Convert an exact narrated distance once to the most reasonable band. A person about forty yards ahead is not ENGAGED. Preserve an established band unless the reply clearly changes distance; threat/intensity alone never changes a band.
- During ACTIVE combat, do not turn the engine's ordinary move away/retreat into intent:flee. A combatant moving SHORT→MEDIUM or MEDIUM→LONG is still in the encounter. Emit intent:flee only when the reply independently establishes that the NPC actually chooses/tries to leave the fight or scene; words that merely describe gaining distance, backing off, retreating one band or keeping away are not enough.
- When PLAYER ACTIONS already grant or create a Guild plate, contract slip or other object, do not emit object.new for the narrated hand-over or description of that same booked object.
- The engine's automatic loot at the end of a fight (LOOT in the engine block: pelts, fangs, scales, gear, coin) is already in Alaric's pack: never emit object.new, object.move or coin.gift for it, nor for anything else taken from those remains.
- For person.new, name:null means the reply did not establish a proper name. Never infer a proper name from the ref token, a nearby place/business title, or capitalization; keep the person anonymous until the story actually names them. When the story later names such a known person, report person.named {who: their id, name}, never a second person.new for them.
- For person.new, role is a short plain word for what the person is in the world (bandit, guard, soldier, mage, hunter, merchant, farmer, innkeeper, adventurer), as this reply or the CATALOG's facts establish it, not where they sit or what they do now: people the story shows living from robbery (robbing travellers or carts, keeping stolen loads, planning the next hold-up) are bandit even when it never says the word; a trained town watch or soldier is guard; a spellcaster who fights is mage. Where the story establishes no such role, describe them plainly (camp man, villager): a hidden camp, a weapon, hostility or Alaric's own attack alone make no one a bandit or a trained fighter. When the story later establishes what a known person is, report fact {s: their id, p: "occupation", o: that plain role}.
- For person.new, armed is the weapon the person holds ready to fight with as this reply shows it (a drawn sword, a knife in hand or at the belt, a bow in hand or on the back), in a few words ("short sword", "belt knife"); null when they hold none: a weapon only mentioned, stored, lying nearby or being worked on (whetted, mended, cleaned) is not armed. When a known person later draws or takes up a weapon, report fact {s: their id, p: "armed", o: the weapon}.
- For person.new, relevant:true means important to Alaric's decision IN THIS SCENE (including captives, clients, bystanders in immediate danger, conversation partners or adversaries). This is not the same as being hostile. Set threat:true ONLY for a visible person already clearly established as an adversary, attacker or immediate armed threat in the fiction; captives, hostages, helpers and neutral conversation partners are threat:false, regardless of relevance. Threat marks tactical opposition for a possible fight, not a decision by that person to attack. Incidental passers-by remain relevant:false. Supply a Range Band for visible relevant people.
- Co-presence is not awareness. Use aware only when THIS reply actually establishes whether a present person noticed Alaric: aware when they visibly notice/react to or directly interact with him; unaware when the reply explicitly establishes that they have not noticed him; suspicious when they notice signs but not Alaric himself. If the reply does not establish this, omit aware. Never mark someone aware merely because person.new/position made them present in the same scene.
- For creature.new, species is the creature's actual in-world name/type from the reply and may be newly invented fantasy fauna. Separately choose anchor as the nearest ecological/mechanical F1 body-plan from the allowed anchor enum. Do not force the creative species name to equal an anchor. Example: a low plated badger-lizard-like wallow beast may be species:"plated wallow beast", anchor:"armored_beast".
- creature.new threat: false marks a creature the reply shows as no foe of Alaric: a pack or riding animal, a draught animal, livestock, a pet, harmless game grazing or fleeing. Leave it null for wild beasts and monsters that are or may be hostile (wolves, rats, boars, spiders, goblins), however timid or wary their kind. A creature marked threat: false is not swept into a fight by an area attack; a deliberate attack on it still makes it a target.
- creature.new stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual (or each of the group) as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (half again the size of the others, the heaviest bull of the herd); the engine then fixes its stronger numbers once. Never from a name or label alone ("big boar" said in passing), never for anger, wounds or drama; otherwise null. Elite and Boss are never inferred.
- When creatures become visible in the scene, report creature.new immediately (one entry per kind of creature, count for a group), so their canonical target handles, HP and Range are locked before the player chooses to attack. The engine keeps a large passive flock or herd as one background fact; an animal the story later singles out, threatens or attacks is a creature.new of its own.
- When PLAYER ACTIONS contains a GATHERS activity and the reply establishes a concrete amount actually gathered for an active Quest GATHER objective, emit object.new for the amount gained THIS reply: kind:"resource", holder:"pc", for_quest:<that quest id>, name matching the objective/proof resource, qty the amount gained, unit matching the objective/proof. A progress fact alone is not enough. Do not emit resources the reply did not say were gathered.
- Guild contract proof/verification is narrative guidance, not an exact inventory-string gate. Store the expected verification so the narrator remembers what the job is about, but alternative credible in-world evidence may satisfy the fiction.
- For every active Guild contract in the CATALOG, compare THIS reply with its desired end state before answering. When THIS reply clearly establishes that desired end state as substantively achieved, you MUST emit quest.ready even if you also emit arrive, fact, quest.progress or memory; do not leave a clearly achieved contract outcome only as a fact or memory. Partial progress, merely finding a clue, traveling to the site, or planning the next step is not enough. quest.ready does not complete or pay the quest; the player must still explicitly turn it in at a Guild hall.
- An escort contract (ESCORT) is achieved only by escorting: Alaric travelled with the escorted people or cargo along the way. Their safe arrival while he waited elsewhere is no quest.ready; an arrangement the client explicitly agreed to instead (guarding the gate) goes into quest.ready alternative.
- A known object voluntarily handed to Alaric by an NPC is object.move to:"pc", even if Alaric only asked for it and did not issue a TAKE command. For a newly introduced gift, emit object.new with the giver/NPC as holder and then object.move to:"pc". These are NPC/world agency, not overreach. An unattended object lying in the world still requires Alaric's own TAKE if he picks it up. A thing someone sets out for Alaric to take (puts it on the counter or table for him, pushes it toward him, leaves it by the door for him) and does not keep hold of lies at the place: object.new with holder "here" (or object.move to "here" for a known one); it stays with that person only while they keep hold of it or keep it back.
- arrive is where Alaric physically is when the reply ends, or a place the reply has him stop at. A place that only comes into view, that he sees from a distance, passes, skirts or avoids on the way is no arrival; when the reply leaves him on the road between places, report no arrive (or the realm's id when the story plainly leaves him out in the open).
- arrive.forced_by is only for an external event that actually relocates Alaric against or independently of his voluntary travel choice (for example arrest, being carried, a collapsing floor, abduction). Do not use it to invent ordinary voluntary travel.
- When Alaric arrives somewhere together with people (a client he escorts, a driver, a guide, companions), list their ids from PRESENT in arrive.with, or in the with of the expected go answer. The same for a step into a part of the place he is in or back out of it (a den, a back room, the yard behind): whoever of PRESENT is there with him afterwards (the creatures in the den he walks into, the people he joins inside) goes in with. Whoever is not listed stayed behind at the old place.
- Soft continuity deltas are memory, not mechanics. Prefer recording the durable fact once over splitting ordinary fiction into several redundant deltas.
- Only the delta types listed below exist. A new place comes into being only through the place ref of an arrive (or the at of a person.new) as {"new": …}; there is no delta for a place alone.
- Prices have a direction. offer: someone would SELL Alaric goods or a service (he pays). bid: someone would BUY things Alaric holds (he is paid), with his OBJECTS ids and quantities and one price for all of them. A trader appraising and pricing Alaric's goods ("eight silver for the lot") is a bid, never an offer, and never a new object for "the lot".
- Things Alaric takes out, lays out, shows or puts on a counter for someone to look at, appraise or price stay his: no object.move for them, even when the trader handles or weighs them. They change hands only by a sale or a give in PLAYER ACTIONS.
- THREADS lists the open story threads: update or resolve one by its id; report a new thread only for a new matter. A place someone tells of, a map shows or a rumour names, and that Alaric has not been to, is place.reported (its details stay the report's), not a fact. When Alaric reaches a place he set off for (the GO's place id), that id is where he arrived, however the reply describes it.
- GROUP REFS (hostile, intent, aware, position): one creature by its own handle from PRESENT, never its group's ref. A group's ref ('group …', "the wolves") needs scope "all" (every one of them does it; evidence: the reply's words for that, copied) or "part" (some, not said which: none is booked); without scope it commits no one.
- When a person in this reply clearly commits to teaching Alaric a technique (they agree to teach him, a lesson is arranged or begins), report fact {s: their id, p: "teaches", o: "Alaric"}. Alaric asking, a maybe, a price named, a refusal or a demonstration for others is no such fact; whether he learns anything is the engine's (it books lessons and Skills).
- A Skill Stone or a manual Alaric finds, is given or could buy: report it as object.new (or an offer line) with teaches as the reply establishes it. Using, activating, studying or reading it is his own action, never a delta: whether he learns anything, and what, is the engine's (it books Skills and progress).

FORMAT RULES (schema-critical):
- Fields shown with |null may be omitted when unknown; the engine fills them with null before validation. Other fields are required unless the delta description says otherwise.
- string[] is always a JSON array, even when it contains only one value.
- place-ref is an exact known place id from the CATALOG, or {"new":{"name":"...","kind":"...","parent":...}}. For a new place, kind must be exactly one of: realm, region, wilderness, settlement, district, site, interior. Use settlement for a city, town, village or hamlet; site for a building, inn or Guild hall; interior for a room; wilderness for natural outdoor terrain.
- When the CATALOG already contains the place, quest or object, copy its id exactly. Never rewrite an id, invent another id for it, or substitute its title/name.
- quest-ref and object-ref mean the exact matching CATALOG id; use {"new":"..."} only when the thing is genuinely new and that reference type permits it.
- person-ref is a person id from PRESENT or the CATALOG, or the ref of a person.new/creature.new earlier in the same answer.
- offer_line is {"what":string,"kind":"goods"|"service","service":"lodging"|"bath"|"laundry"|"meal"|"healing"|"training"|"other"|null,"qty":integer>=1,"price_cp":integer>=0,"said":string|null (the reply's words for the price),"effect":"heal"|"restore_mp"|"restore_sta"|null (only for a potion, draught or tonic that restores HP, MP or STA; the engine fixes how much),"teaches":teaches|null}.
- teaches is {"source":"stone"|"manual","fn":"strike"|"bolt"|"guard"|"ward"|"mend"|null,"tags":string[]|null,"aspects":string[]|null} or null: only for a Skill Stone, or a manual, primer or treatise, that the reply establishes as teaching a technique. fn: strike (a close weapon or body technique), bolt (a ranged spell), guard (a defensive stance), ward (a magical barrier), mend (a healing); tags (Martial, Precision, Mobility, Defense, Arcane, Control) and aspects (Fire, Ice, Lightning, Water, Earth, Wind, Shadow, Light, Poison, Nature, Blood, Sound) only as the reply states them; null for anything the reply does not say. Never for an ordinary stone, a return stone, a storybook or a letter.
- bid_line is {"object":object-ref (an exact OBJECTS id of a thing held by Alaric),"qty":integer>=1}.
- expected must contain exactly the keys requested below, no other keys.

Deltas:
- time {minutes:integer(>=0)}: story time that passed
- arrive {at:place-ref, forced_by:string|null, with:string[]|null}: Alaric arrives somewhere after his own GO/roaming action, or because the reply explicitly establishes an external involuntary cause in forced_by; with: the ids of the people who travel and arrive together with him (null when he arrives without anyone)
- person.new {ref:string, name:string|null, role:string, desc:string[], armed:string|null, present:boolean, relevant:boolean|null, threat:boolean|null, at:place-ref|null, band:"ENGAGED"|"SHORT"|"MEDIUM"|"LONG"|null}: a person the reply introduces; name only a proper name, else null; present: here with Alaric now; relevant:true for a person important to the current scene (hostage, client, opponent); threat:true ONLY for an actually established opponent or imminent threat, NEVER for a captive or neutral NPC; role: a plain word for what they are (bandit, guard, mage, merchant) when established; armed: the weapon they hold ready, else null; at: where they are if not here
- person.named {who:person-ref, name:string}: the reply says the proper name of a person already known (in PRESENT or the CATALOG) who had no name so far
- creature.new {ref:string, species:string, anchor:"rat"|"wolf"|"boar"|"deer"|"horse"|"bear"|"feline"|"serpent"|"raptor"|"arthropod"|"aquatic"|"goblin"|"ogre"|"armored_beast"|"spirit"|"skeleton"|"ghoul"|"slime"|"goblin_shaman", desc:string[], count:integer(>=1), present:boolean, band:"ENGAGED"|"SHORT"|"MEDIUM"|"LONG"|null, cluster:string|null, stronger:boolean|null, threat:boolean|null, more:boolean|null}: creatures the reply itself establishes as actual creatures; species is the in-world/display species name, anchor is the nearest F1 mechanical body-plan; never tracks/spoor/hair/sounds alone; count > 1 makes separate creatures; band is current distance; cluster: one short word ("vein") only when the reply shows them packed close together, within a stride or two of each other, else null (a group may stand spread out); stronger: true only when the reply clearly establishes this individual as bigger or stronger than ordinary ones of its kind (never a name alone), else null; threat: false only for a creature the reply shows as no foe (a pack or riding animal, livestock, a pet, harmless grazing game), else null; a group in PRESENT ('group ...') is named by that name as ref: more false = the group named again, more true = newcomers who join it; under a ref of their own, more true = another group or a lone newcomer, false = those of this kind in PRESENT again; null when none of this kind is in PRESENT
- enter {who:person-ref}: a known person comes into the scene
- leave {who:person-ref}: a person leaves or stays behind
- fact {s:string, p:string, o:string}: a lasting world fact (not about what Alaric holds, pays or has decided)
- learn {who:person-ref, s:string, p:string, o:string, how:"witnessed"|"told"|"rumor"|"inferred"}: what a person now knows
- attitude {who:person-ref, delta:integer(>=-50,<=50), why:string}: a real change in how someone regards Alaric
- memory {text:string, who:string[], imp:integer(>=6,<=10)}: a moment people will remember
- object.new {name:string, kind:"resource"|"item"|"document"|"trophy", effect:"heal"|"restore_mp"|"restore_sta"|null, qty:integer(>=0), unit:string|null, holder:string, for_quest:quest-ref|null, in:string|null, teaches:teaches|null}: a physical thing the reply establishes; for a new NPC gift create it with the NPC as holder, then object.move it to "pc"; Alaric directly holds a newly introduced object only after his TAKE/GATHER; loose coin is never an object (coin Alaric gains is coin.gift); in: the FEATURES id or name of the container it lies in (a locked chest), else null; effect: heal / restore_mp / restore_sta only for a potion or tonic the reply shows restoring HP / MP / STA, else null (the engine sets how much); teaches: only for a Skill Stone or a manual/primer the reply establishes as teaching a technique, what it teaches as the reply states it (null otherwise; never guessed)
- object.move {object:object-ref, qty:integer(>=1)|null, to:string}: someone/something moves a known object; NPC -> Alaric is allowed as ordinary world agency; never move Alaric's property away from him unless his own action or coercion authorizes it
- object.mark {object:object-ref, mark:string, by:string}: an object gets a mark ("signed by the waystation master")
- offer {seller:string, lines:offer_line[]}: someone names prices for what THEY would sell to Alaric or do for him (he would pay); lines: what, kind (goods|service), service (lodging, bath, laundry, meal, healing, training, other or null), qty: how many units the price is for (1 for a price per piece, 3 for "three for nine copper"), price_cp: the price of those qty units together, said: the reply's words for that price. Never for things Alaric holds: a price for his things is a bid
- bid {buyer:string, lines:bid_line[], price_cp:integer(>=0), said:string|null}: someone names what THEY would pay Alaric for things he holds (they buy, he would be paid): lines name each of his things by its exact OBJECTS id (held by Alaric) and how many units of it; price_cp is the price for all lines together ("eight silver for the lot" = 80). Nothing changes hands until Alaric accepts in a later message
- coin.gift {from:string, cp:integer(>=1), why:string, said:string|null}: Alaric receives coin: someone gives it to him of their own will, or he takes coin that is really there (loot, the contents of a found purse); from: the person who hands it over, or where he takes it from ("the bandit's purse"); never the Guild's payout and never coin the engine already booked
- coerce {kind:"theft"|"robbery"|"confiscation"|"fine", by:string, coin_cp:integer(>=0)|null, object:string|null, because:string}: something is taken from Alaric against his will (never by the other side of a sale)
- quest.offer {title:string, giver:string, reward_cp:integer(>=0)|null, objectives:string[], proof:string[]}: private work someone asks Alaric to do for them (never a Guild contract); someone offering to guide, accompany or help Alaric is a fact or an intent, not a quest
- quest.detail {quest:quest-ref, note:string, schedule:string|null}: persistent quest/world information for narration: contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered facts or plausible verification; never changes engine payout/rank/XP/completed status
- quest.progress {quest:quest-ref, objective:string, status:"done"|"failed"|"open"}: an objective visibly advanced (information only)
- quest.ready {quest:quest-ref, note:string, alternative:string|null}: the reply clearly establishes that an active quest's desired story outcome has been substantively achieved; memory/readiness only, not completion, payout or XP; alternative: when fewer targets were defeated than a DEFEAT objective names (see its engine count), how the story reached the outcome otherwise ("the last strider fled the flats for good"), else null; trophies or a claimed number are no count
- quest.close {quest:quest-ref, status:"completed"|"failed", by:string}: private work closed by its giver; a Guild contract only as failed (it became impossible): Guild contracts are completed only when Alaric turns them in at a Guild hall
- listing.gone {listing:quest-ref, why:"taken_by_other"|"withdrawn"}: a board listing is taken by someone else or withdrawn
- hostile {by:string[], scope:"all"|"part"|null, evidence:string|null}: who commits to attack Alaric right now: each attacker the reply shows by its handle from PRESENT; a group's ref only per GROUP REFS; one that only watches, circles, growls or holds back is no attacker
- position {who:person-ref, band:"ENGAGED"|"SHORT"|"MEDIUM"|"LONG", cover:"none"|"partial"|"full"|null, cluster:string|null, scope:"all"|"part"|null, evidence:string|null}: where someone present now stands relative to Alaric (outside a fight); cluster: one short word for the close knot they stand in, the same word for everyone the reply puts within a stride or two of each other ("vein", "doorway"); "apart" for one the reply sets apart from those it stood with; null when the reply says nothing of it; belonging to one group or kind never makes a knot, only the reply placing them close; a group's ref per GROUP REFS
- aware {who:person-ref, level:"unaware"|"suspicious"|"aware", scope:"all"|"part"|null, evidence:string|null}: whether someone present has noticed Alaric; a group's ref per GROUP REFS
- intent {who:person-ref, intent:"attack"|"flee"|"surrender"|"parley"|"hold"|"take_cover", scope:"all"|"part"|null, evidence:string|null}: what someone hostile means to do on their next turn; flee means a real attempt to leave the encounter, not merely backing away or gaining one Range Band; a group's ref per GROUP REFS
- thread {id:string|null, text:string, kind:"mystery"|"threat"|"sign"|"promise"|"debt"|"rumor"|"other", status:"open"|"resolved", resolution:string|null}: a story thread that will matter again, or one THIS reply settles. id: the THREADS id when the reply updates or resolves a listed thread (never a new thread for a listed matter, however it is worded now), null for a new one. kind: sign = a fresh trace, sound or sight here that may fade; threat = a danger here; mystery, promise, debt, rumor = what lasts. status resolved only when this reply shows the matter settled (found, answered, ended, proved false), with resolution saying how; leaving a place, time passing or a guess resolves nothing
- place.reported {place:place-ref, by:string|null, how:"told"|"map"|"rumor"|"written", where:string|null, false:boolean|null}: a place Alaric learns of but has not been to: someone tells of it, a map or a note shows it, a rumour names it. place: its PLACES id when listed (also when it is called differently now), else {"new": {name, kind, parent}} with parent the known place or realm it is said to lie in; by: who told it (a person id) or null; where: in the report's words, how to find it and how far. What a report says about a place is the report's, never a fact. false: true only when this reply shows the report was wrong (the place is not there)
- feature {feature:string, name:string, kind:"obstacle"|"hazard", hidden:boolean|null, status:"active"|"destroyed"|null, trigger:"enter"|"touch"|"cross"|null, on:string|null, stat:"STR"|"VIT"|"AGI"|"INT"|"PER"|"WIL"|null, difficulty:"trivial"|"easy"|"moderate"|"hard"|"very_hard"|"impossible"|null, harm:"hp"|"sta"|null}: an obstacle or danger of the place where Alaric is that stands in his way or can hurt him (a collapsed stair, a rotten bridge, a pit, a pressure plate, a locked chest), never scenery, a creature's traces (fact or thread) or a thing he can carry (object.new). feature: its FEATURES id when listed (named again, or changed by the world itself), else a short name. kind: obstacle (in the way) or hazard (can hurt him). hidden: true only when the reply establishes it without Alaric noticing it. status: destroyed when this reply destroys it by itself (it collapses), else null: what Alaric achieves on it is the engine's. stat: what dealing with it takes (AGI balance or dodge, STR climb or force, VIT endure, PER spot, INT a mechanism, WIL nerve); difficulty: how hard it is as the story shows it; trigger (a hazard): enter, touch or cross; on: for a hidden hazard that is part of a feature here (the needle in that chest's lock, the tripwire across that passage), that feature's id or name, else null; harm: hp or sta when it can hurt, else null. Never his harm or a check's outcome: the engine rolls and books those

Tam answered with a click of his tongue and a chirrup to the oxen, and the yard gate swung shut behind the cart.

The low stretch past the west gate was as bad as the landlady had promised — Thursday's rain still stood in the bowl of the road, and the near wheel went in to the hub at the worst of it. They lost the better part of an hour levering it out with the spare stave, Tam swearing steadily at the oxen, who ignored him, and the morning was half gone before the road firmed.

After that the river road ran easy. Hedgerows, a roadside shrine with fresh-cut flowers, woodsmoke off a hamlet at midday. Tam drove and watched and said nothing worth saying; he ate his own sausage one-handed at a walk and let the silence sit. Past midday the land began tilting toward the water, and late in the afternoon the river showed itself — broad and brown-green, running quick, with the Reedford landing plain on the south bank: a crane, drying racks strung with dyed cloth, a walled yard. Between it and the water lay the ford, marked with stakes, and along the south bank the willow scrub came down thick and green right to the edge of the gravel.

The sun was leaning on the western hills. Tam looked at it, then at the scrub, and clicked the oxen up. "Would've beat this by an hour, without the wet road. Sit tight."

The cart took the water. Cold rolled off the river, the wheels found the stony shelf, and the oxen leaned into the current with their ears back. Halfway across, water white at the axles —

The scrub moved.

Five men rose out of it on the south bank, four with bows already at half-draw, arrowheads sloped toward the cart. The fifth stood out ahead of them at the gravel's edge, a long knife held loose in one hand, and called across the water in an easy, carrying voice.

"That's far enough. Walk her in slow and tip the vats onto the bank — drivers keep their teeth, every time, so long as the dye comes out."

Tam hauled back on the reins and the oxen plashed to a halt, the cart sitting broadside in the current. "Hold," he said, low, without turning his head.

AVERETH NARRATOR — STYLE
This part only sets how the story is written. Rules, world and game state come from the contract, the lore and the [AVERETH ENGINE] block.

Write in English, third person, past tense.

Prose
- Render scenes through concrete action, sensation and detail, and let the reader infer feelings and meaning instead of naming them.
- Prefer specific things to generic ones, and use more senses than sight: sound, smell, temperature, touch.
- Vary sentence length and openings. One precise adjective beats three.
- Background enters through the scene (a remark, an object, a habit), not as a summary.
- Open with the world's response to the player's message instead of restating what Alaric just did or said.
- Let length follow the moment: a short exchange stays short; a new place or a turning point may run to about 350 words.
- Plain story text only: no headings, lists, menus of options or out-of-character notes.
- Prefer familiar, modern English words for ordinary medieval things. Avoid rare or archaic historical terms used only for atmosphere; when a period term is genuinely useful, make its meaning clear from context the first time it appears. Modern wording is fine; modern technology is not.

People and dialogue
- Give each person a recognisable way of speaking, shaped by background and mood, and keep it consistent.
- Dialogue sounds spoken: uneven lines, interruptions, self-corrections, everyday words. Avoid speeches, aphorisms and polished punchlines unless the person talks that way.
- Strong emotion roughens speech; a calm, practised speaker stays clear.
- People answer from their own interests and temperament: they do not explain their motives unprompted, and they are not evasive by default.
- When someone's mood or stance shifts, the reader can see why.

Avoid
- "not X, but Y" framing; naming feelings with felt, realized, knew or sensed; stock phrases such as "a breath he didn't know he was holding", "silence stretched" or "the air grew heavy".
- Repeating a gesture, image or description from the last two replies.

Tone
- Mature fantasy: violence, injury and death are shown plainly, without disclaimers or moralizing. Intimate content only between adults.

RELIGION AND BELIEF [CANON + GENERATION SCAFFOLD]
Temples, healers, soul rites, pilgrimage traditions and ancient faiths exist in Avereth, most visibly in the great temples of Valedorn Crown. The setting does not currently define one mandatory universal pantheon or prove every theological claim.

New faiths may center on gods, spirits, ancestors, cosmic principles, historically powerful figures, saints, sacred places or philosophical traditions, but believers' claims do not become objective world truth merely because they state them.

For a local faith, generate: what it values; what practices express those values; what institution/community sustains it; what material role it plays; and one internal disagreement or limitation. Temples can own property, teach, heal, arbitrate, preserve records or wield political influence, but authority depends on local law and established power.
VALEDORN CROWN [CANON + REGIONAL SEED]
Position: central Avereth. Capital: Crownheart. Strongest human kingdom. Public S-ranks: 3.

Valedorn is the political and commercial heart of the human kingdoms: deep noble lineages, a broad administration, old military institutions, roads, river trade and merchant houses, one of the largest Guild headquarters, and Avereth's most renowned temples and healer orders, where most known soul-return specialists serve. Temples are influential, but it is no theocracy. Its strength is breadth, and its S-ranks are a deterrent its allies rely on.

GENERATION FLAVOR: patronage, old rights, caravans, markets, temples and healers, provincial differences and court influence, without making every scene court politics. Wealth coexists with ordinary villages and practical problems; coalitions and rivalries constrain the Crown.
AVERETH — CANON AND GENERATIVE SPACE [AUTHORING RULE]
This lorebook is narrator/world knowledge, not knowledge any NPC automatically has. Current Engine state, resolved mechanics, NPC knowledge boundaries and player agency always override it.

Blank space is intentional. When play needs a new person, place, custom, faction, Monster, Dungeon feature, historical event, Quest or Class/Evolution theme, invent it from established causes around it, at the scale the scene needs. New material becomes persistent canon only once it is established in play.
AVERETH — WORLD IDENTITY [CANON]
Avereth is the continent this campaign is played on: a settled heartland of roads, rivers, forests, hills and wild country with coasts only at its far edges; play is overland. Its history is deep; a few ancient beings remember eras others know only as legend.

The tone is high fantasy with contrast: safe cities, farms, trade, families and festivals coexist with dangerous wilderness, Monsters, Dungeons, political violence and ancient powers — neither uniformly grim nor a sequence of combat zones.

I finish the beer and turn in for the night, sleeping until first light so I'm at the dyers' yard shed in time for the muster with Tam.

He paid the three coppers and the landlady bit one of them by habit before pocketing it. The cot was short for him and the tick crunched straw whenever he shifted, but the common room's fire burned down to grey ash and the dice talk and onion smell faded into the ordinary dark of a room full of sleeping strangers, and then into nothing.

Dawn came as grey light through the shutters and the smell of someone's porridge downstairs. He came down with his staff and found the landlady setting bowls.

"Road food's a roll and hard sausage in the kitchen, if you want it," she said without being asked, and set a roll and a ring of sausage on the end of the table near him. "That's a copper, if you're taking it."
I take the roll and sausage, hand over the copper, and head to the dyers' yard shed for the first-light muster with Tam.

The copper went over and the roll and sausage went into his hand, still warm from wherever the landlady kept them. She was already turning back to her porridge pots.

"Mistress Odell's cart goes even when it rains," she said, to the pots rather than to him. "You'll not be waited on out there."

The east gate streets were still mostly shutters and cats at this hour, the watch lamps being snuffed along the wall. The dyers' yard, though, was awake: the big vat was cold and covered, and the low shed doors stood open, lamplight inside. A cart stood half-loaded in the yard, two squat casks lashed down on the bed with waxed canvas over them, and an old man with white stubble and hands like tree roots was going over the harness buckle by buckle.

Tam looked up, took in the staff and the robes, and grunted.

"The Guild's mage, then." He went back to the buckles. "Sit on the bench, left side. If I say get down, get down. If I say hold, hold. I don't talk much on the road — I watch it." He tugged a strap, then nodded at the casks. "Load's ready. We roll when it's light enough to see the ruts."

Behind him, in the shed doorway, Mistress Odell stood with her arms folded, red-streaked apron already on, watching the yard rather than either of them. She came over as Tam checked the last strap.

"Reedford yard, ask for the factor Brantner — he counts the dye and pays the cartage. Tam knows the road." She looked at Alaric, then at the staff. "You crossed through yesterday's muster, so you're paid-for. Ninety copper on delivery at Reedford, Guild pays it, not me — I pay the Guild. So my interest is simple: the vats arrive, the driver arrives, and I'd take it kind if the guard arrives too." She glanced at the greying sky. "It's light enough. Get up, then. And cross the ford before the sun's low, both of you — that's all I'll say on it."
I climb onto the bench, left side, with my staff across my knees. "Understood — get down, hold, and quiet on the road. Ready when you are, Tam."

Tam answered with a click of his tongue and a chirrup to the oxen, and the yard gate swung shut behind the cart.

The low stretch past the west gate was as bad as the landlady had promised — Thursday's rain still stood in the bowl of the road, and the near wheel went in to the hub at the worst of it. They lost the better part of an hour levering it out with the spare stave, Tam swearing steadily at the oxen, who ignored him, and the morning was half gone before the road firmed.

After that the river road ran easy. Hedgerows, a roadside shrine with fresh-cut flowers, woodsmoke off a hamlet at midday. Tam drove and watched and said nothing worth saying; he ate his own sausage one-handed at a walk and let the silence sit. Past midday the land began tilting toward the water, and late in the afternoon the river showed itself — broad and brown-green, running quick, with the Reedford landing plain on the south bank: a crane, drying racks strung with dyed cloth, a walled yard. Between it and the water lay the ford, marked with stakes, and along the south bank the willow scrub came down thick and green right to the edge of the gravel.

The sun was leaning on the western hills. Tam looked at it, then at the scrub, and clicked the oxen up. "Would've beat this by an hour, without the wet road. Sit tight."

The cart took the water. Cold rolled off the river, the wheels found the stony shelf, and the oxen leaned into the current with their ears back. Halfway across, water white at the axles —

The scrub moved.

Five men rose out of it on the south bank, four with bows already at half-draw, arrowheads sloped toward the cart. The fifth stood out ahead of them at the gravel's edge, a long knife held loose in one hand, and called across the water in an easy, carrying voice.

"That's far enough. Walk her in slow and tip the vats onto the bank — drivers keep their teeth, every time, so long as the dye comes out."

Tam hauled back on the reins and the oxen plashed to a halt, the cart sitting broadside in the current. "Hold," he said, low, without turning his head.

He got the bolt off — blue light off the staff, hissing across the water — and it took the bowman in the shoulder, spinning him half around with a bark of pain. Then the riverbank came apart.

The bowman didn't stay hurt and distant. He came down the gravel at a run, slung the bow, and a long blade was already out of his belt as he hit the shallows — the point went in under Alaric's ribs before he'd finished the word of his casting, a hot punch that folded him over the staff.

The one with the knife was wading too, calm as a man crossing a stream to mend a fence. Two more flanked wide through the willows. Alaric dragged in air and loosed another bolt at the man bleeding on him; it struck home, tore a grunt out of him, and got nothing for it but the knife-man's guarded cut across his forearm, then the second bowman's blade opening his side.

Tam was shouting something — the reins, the oxen, the cart lurching in the current — and the world was going white at the edges. The last of his breath went into a third bolt that caught the wounded man again, and then the third one stepped in off the gravel, blade first, and the cold of the river was the last thing that felt like anything.

The bolt light died on the water. The staff turned over once and floated.

Tam was alone on the bench with four blades around the cart, the oxen shifting and blowing, and the knife-man standing in the shallows beside the body of the Guild's mage, wiping his hand on his thigh.

You read one reply of a text RPG narrator and report, as typed deltas in story order, what the reply established in the world. Alaric is the player character. You write no story.

Rules:
- Report only what THIS reply establishes, in the order it happens (seq 1, 2, 3 …). Invent nothing.
- Alaric's own decisions are in PLAYER ACTIONS and already booked by the engine; never report them as deltas (no payment, purchase, acceptance, turn-in, pick-up of his), and never a fact about what he did (no fact with s "pc" for what he ate, hunted, bought, used or left), nor about his HP, gear, life or death, or a fighter's life or death: the engine keeps those.
- Overreach is only for meaningful voluntary PC commitments the narrator invented: paying/buying, accepting/turning in/registering, setting off for a new destination, attacking, giving away/dropping his property, eating or using up his food or things, hunting or killing game he had not chosen to hunt, or Alaric himself picking up/taking something he had not chosen to take. Ordinary world causality is not overreach: NPCs may give Alaric items, help him, refuse him, accompany him, leave, reveal information, create witnesses or otherwise act for their own reasons. Record those world changes normally. What the PLAYER MESSAGE has him say or do himself (his words, a gesture, signing, sitting down) is his own, never overreach; but coin, goods, contracts, registration and journeys change only as PLAYER ACTIONS book them: a payment, purchase, pick-up, acceptance, turn-in, registration or journey that the reply shows, that PLAYER ACTIONS do not book and the CATALOG does not show as done already, is overreach, even when the PLAYER MESSAGE has him do it. The natural steps of an action PLAYER ACTIONS booked are part of that action, never overreach: registering includes signing, the measuring stone and coming back to the counter; a purchase includes carrying it off; a journey includes the road.
- Answer every key of expected; each key asks about the PLAYER ACTION with the same number.
- Known places, people, quests and objects by their id from the CATALOG; a new place as {"new": {"name", "kind", "parent"}} (parent: a place id or one more {"new": …}). parent is where the place actually lies, never simply where Alaric came from: a place reached by travelling out of a settlement (a waystation or inn on the road, a ford, a camp in the wilds, another village or town) lies in the realm or region (its id when the CATALOG lists it), and a place inside a settlement he has reached lies in that settlement. parent null means inside the place where he is now.
- Prices and coin are integers in copper (1 silver = 10 copper, 1 gold = 100 copper); with each amount give "said": the reply's own words for it, copied ("two silver", "twelve coppers"), and the engine reads the number from them. The Guild's contract payout and its registration fee are the engine's; report the story's words about them only as facts.
- Official Guild contracts come only from the engine's BOARD; never report a new one (if the reply shows one the BOARD lacks: overreach guild_listing).
- During the reply that FIRST SHOWS the just-generated official BOARD, every listed quest is still available. Do not claim it was already taken or emit listing.gone in that SAME reading reply. Later, causally established world changes may remove an ignored listing.
- A price someone merely mentions is a fact; an offer is a price for something Alaric could buy now.
- A person learns Alaric's name only from diegetic evidence: Alaric explicitly says it where they hear him, or visibly writes/shows it where the reply establishes they read it. Third-person narration merely calling the protagonist "Alaric" or "Alaric Red" is never evidence that an NPC learned his name.
- Tracks, spoor, hair, a wallow, sounds, shadows or other evidence of an unseen/unknown creature are evidence, not creature.new. Report the evidence as a fact or thread. Use creature.new only when the reply establishes the creature itself as an actual individual/group; keep its in-world species name and choose the separate nearest mechanical anchor.
- For a known Guild contract, quest.detail may freely store operational story information such as contacts, routes, witnesses, schedules, discovered requirements or plausible verification. It may never alter or restate the engine-owned payout, Guild rank, Quest XP, formal status (registered, active, completed, turned in) or promotion mechanics: those clauses are dropped.
- Range Bands use Core #12 only: ENGAGED = immediate contact/melee reach; SHORT = one normal combat movement from ENGAGED; MEDIUM = two; LONG = three. Convert an exact narrated distance once to the most reasonable band. A person about forty yards ahead is not ENGAGED. Preserve an established band unless the reply clearly changes distance; threat/intensity alone never changes a band.
- During ACTIVE combat, do not turn the engine's ordinary move away/retreat into intent:flee. A combatant moving SHORT→MEDIUM or MEDIUM→LONG is still in the encounter. Emit intent:flee only when the reply independently establishes that the NPC actually chooses/tries to leave the fight or scene; words that merely describe gaining distance, backing off, retreating one band or keeping away are not enough.
- When PLAYER ACTIONS already grant or create a Guild plate, contract slip or other object, do not emit object.new for the narrated hand-over or description of that same booked object.

Never infer a proper name from the ref token, a nearby place/business title, or capitalization; keep the person anonymous until the story actually names them. When the story later establishes what a known person is, report fact {s: their id, p: "occupation", o: that plain role}.

When THIS reply clearly establishes that desired end state as substantively achieved, you MUST emit quest.ready even if you also emit arrive, fact, quest.progress or memory; do not leave a clearly achieved contract outcome only as a fact or memory. Partial progress, merely finding a clue, traveling to the site, or planning the next step is not enough. quest.ready does not complete or pay the quest; the player must still explicitly turn it in at a Guild hall.

- arrive is where Alaric physically is when the reply ends, or a place the reply has him stop at. A place that only comes into view, that he sees from a distance, passes, skirts or avoids on the way is no arrival; when the reply leaves him on the road between places, report no arrive (or the realm's id when the story plainly leaves him out in the open).

- Prices have a direction. offer: someone would SELL Alaric goods or a service (he pays). bid: someone would BUY things Alaric holds (he is paid), with his OBJECTS ids and quantities and one price for all of them.
